Description: Ingests training data from Garmin (binary .FIT parsing + MTP device sync) and Strava (OAuth API, with cross-source duplicate detection), and body-composition data from Withings (OAuth API) — all stored in a single local SQLite database with a soft-delete/trash/purge model, so nothing is ever silently or permanently lost. Exists to be the single, privacy-preserving source of truth the rest of the app reads from.

A local-only HTTP API (port 3001) exposing activities, body measurements, sync triggers, settings, and the workout-classifier workflow to the frontend. Exists as the sole interface between the local database and the dashboard UI — nothing else talks to the database directly.

A five-tab React dashboard (Overview & Trends, Activities, Body, Data & Sync, Settings) presenting training and body data together, including the training-km-vs-weight correlation view. Exists to make the ingested data actually usable day to day, without needing to open two separate vendor apps.

Classifies running activities into six categories (Recovery Run, Long Session, Repeats/Intervals, Progressive Run, Fartlek, Tapasciata) via either a local LLM (Ollama) or a deterministic statistical method, with a human review/approve/correct workflow before either result is treated as ground truth. Exists to save the manual effort of labeling every run's training intent by hand, while keeping a human in the loop and never sending data off-device.

From-scratch decoder for Garmin's binary .FIT format (session summaries + per-second track points + developer-field extensions), cross-validated on import against a second independent parser as a sanity check only. Exists because no maintained vendor SDK covers this without a cloud dependency.

Copies new .FIT files off the watch via a PowerShell/MTP bridge, parses them, and imports them into SQLite; archives raw files permanently. Exists to get training data off the device without Garmin Connect / any cloud round-trip.

In-app popup and standalone-CLI OAuth2 flows for connecting a Withings account, with automatic token refresh. Exists so body-composition data can be pulled without hosting a public OAuth callback server.
Incremental fetch of weight/fat%/muscle mass/hydration/bone mass/BMI/HR measurements into SQLite. Exists to bring body-composition history into the same local store as training data.

OAuth2 flow (with rotating refresh tokens) plus activity + GPS/HR stream sync, including cross-source duplicate detection against existing Garmin activities. Exists as a second training-data source for activities not captured by the watch/MTP path, without double-counting activities Garmin already uploaded to Strava.

Local database schema for activities, track points, and body measurements, with a two-stage delete model (trash → restore, or purge → permanent) instead of hard deletes. Exists to make "delete" a safe, reversible local action, matching the app's privacy-first, no-cloud-backup design.
REST endpoints for activity list/detail/summary/weekly/monthly aggregates and full per-activity track data. Exists as the read path the Activities and Overview tabs are built on.

REST endpoints for body-measurement list/monthly aggregates and the weekly-running-km-vs-avg-weight correlation query. Exists to compute the "holistic" training/body correlation server-side, once, rather than in the browser.

REST endpoints for Strava OAuth status, login-URL generation, callback handling, and triggering a sync. Exists to let the frontend drive the Strava connection without embedding OAuth logic client-side.

REST endpoints for outlier-detection thresholds, trend-grouping thresholds, theme, background, and measurement-unit preferences, persisted server-side. Exists so user preferences survive across devices/browsers without relying on browser storage.

REST endpoints to run a classification (AI or statistical), record human feedback (approve/reject/correct), and bulk-confirm results. Exists as the backend contract the classifier UI (AI-assisted workout classification epic) is built against.
Tab-based navigation, global date-range selection, and Garmin/Withings/Strava connection-status indicators shared across all tabs. Exists as the scaffolding every other tab plugs into.

Per-sport distance/pace/HR trend charts (single-activity, weekly, or monthly grouping) with reference bands for each sport's average/min/max. Exists to answer "how is my training trending" at a glance, per sport.
Paginated, filterable list of all activities across both training sources. Exists as the entry point for reviewing individual sessions.

Per-activity chart overlaying pace/speed, HR, altitude, cadence, and power, with automatic pause detection and outlier filtering. Exists to give a full, readable picture of a single session beyond its summary numbers.
Body-composition trend charts plus the training-km-vs-weight correlation chart. Exists as the "holistic" centerpiece connecting training volume to body composition on one timeline.

Triggers device-status-gated syncs for all three sources, plus the delete/trash/restore/purge workflow for activities and body measurements. Exists as the one place to manage data lifecycle without touching the database directly.
UI for outlier-detection thresholds, trend-grouping thresholds, theme/background, and measurement-unit preferences. Exists to make the app's behavior configurable without editing config files.
Classifies a run's reduced track-point summary into one of six categories via a locally-running Ollama model. Exists as the higher-nuance classification path, entirely on-device.

Classifies a run using fixed rules over pace variance, splits, and pause pattern — no LLM, instant, no dependency on Ollama being available. Exists as a fast, dependency-free alternative/fallback to the LLM path, and a way to sanity-check it.

Approve/reject/correct UI per activity, with both classification methods' results stored and shown independently so they can be compared before either is confirmed as the activity's final classification. Exists to keep a human in the loop rather than trusting either classifier blindly.
Batch-classify and batch-confirm selected activities from the Data & Sync tab, with per-item progress. Exists to make labeling months of historical activities practical instead of one-by-one.
